sections.kicker: Prepared for Nelissa Hilman by Atla · November 2026
sections.lead: We looked at your Instagram the way a new customer would. Here is what stood out, in order of weight.
sections.thesis: Nelissa Hilman opens its profile with a company number, not with its shoes.
sections.keep: The founder in a white shirt next to a shoebox. It is a recurring image only you own.

sections.label: Front door
title: Three things people
meet first.
Three things
people meet

pins.what: The first line of the bio is a legal registration.
pins.why: A stranger learns the company number before they learn the brand makes shoes and bags.
pins.how: Open with what you make and for whom, and move the legal line down.
pins.label: Your bio
pins.cost: The brand reads as a company, not a point of view.

pins.area: Founder in a white shirt with a shoebox, repeated across four tiles
pins.what: Your strongest image is the founder, not the product.
pins.why: The same person, the same white shirt and the same box make a recognisable face for the brand.
pins.how: Make that image a deliberate, repeating signature.
pins.label: Your grid
pins.cost: The one thing that sets the brand apart appears by accident.

pins.what: Highlight names read as internal codes.
pins.why: A new visitor cannot decode PMxNH, ANYAM03 or RENDA before deciding to follow.
pins.how: Name each highlight for the thing a customer wants to see.
pins.label: Your highlights
pins.cost: Your best stories sit behind labels nobody can read.
